2 Definitions

Adjudication Services means the work carried out by the Adjudicator and the Adjudicator’s Office in dealing with complaints from HMRC and VOA customers.

ADR means an individual mediated Alternative Dispute Resolution activity specifically under HMRC own process.

Agreement means this Service Level Agreement (SLA), including all appendices.

AO means the Adjudicator’s Office.

AO Head of Office means the person with accountability to the Adjudicator for the administration of the AO.

CPD means the Customer, Process, Design Directorate in HMRC.

Conditions mean the terms and conditions in this agreement and in any amendments and variations that may be agreed from time to time between HMRC and the Adjudicator.

Data Protection Legislation has the same meaning as in the Data Protection Act 2018 (see section 3 of that Act).

HMRC means HM Revenue and Customs including the Valuation Office Agency (unless specifically articulated).

The Adjudicator means the Adjudicator for HMRC, including the Valuation Office Agency.

VOA means the Valuation Office Agency.

3 Change history

Not needed for online version.

4 Introduction

4.1 This revised agreement reflects the drive to modernise and improve complaints processes and commitments by both HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) and the Adjudicator.

4.2 The Adjudicator’s terms and conditions are set out in a separate document called the ‘Adjudicator’s terms of appointment’.

4.3 HMRC will provide a support unit and will be responsible for the associated expenditure which will be known as the Adjudicator’s Office (AO).

5 The Adjudicator’s role and remit

5.1 The Adjudicator will provide an independent review of complaints about HMRC to a quality standard in line with industry good practice. In doing so, they will consider if HMRC has provided a fair and consistent application of its published standards, guidance and codes of practice, with the factual evidence of the complaint.

5.2 The Adjudicator falls within the same legal entity as the Commissioners of HMRC, and the staff in the AO are employees of HMRC.

5.3 The Adjudicator is not an employee or an officer of HMRC and is external to HMRC with the independent personal authority to review complaints about HMRC.

5.4 The Adjudicator is an independent and impartial adjudicator of complaints. The independence is preserved by this agreement and the Adjudicator’s terms of appointment. Paragraph 7 of this agreement provides detail around the governance arrangements in place to secure and underpin the independence of both the Adjudicator and the AO in carrying out their role.

5.5 The core purpose of the Adjudicator and the AO is to:

resolve complaints by providing an accessible and flexible service and make fair, trusted and impartial decisions

support and encourage effective resolution throughout the complaints handling process whilst being responsive to customer needs

use insight and expertise to support HMRC to learn from complaints and improve services to customers in line with HMRC’s Charter commitments.

5.6 The Adjudicator’s vision is to work closely with HMRC to achieve the following positive outcomes:

an effective customer-focussed complaint handling service

high-quality, fair decisions regarding complaints

insight which drives action to improve service for customers

5.7 The Adjudicator’s role, purpose and vision have been endorsed by HMRC’s Board and are aligned with HMRC’s complaints and Charter ambition.

5.8 The Adjudicator can only consider complaints from:

the customer (directly affected by the issue raised)

an agent representing the customer (directly affected by the issue raised) - in this situation, the customer must provide written permission for the agent to act on their behalf.

5.9 The Adjudicator can usually only look at complaints which have completed HMRC’s own internal complaints processes.

Complaints can normally only be considered by the AO if brought to them within six months of HMRC’s final Tier 2 response. A decision to make an exception to either of these can only be made by the Adjudicator if they feel there is a compelling and justifiable reason for doing so.

5.10 The Adjudicator can look at complaints about all the following:

mistakes

unreasonable delays

poor or misleading advice

processes

whether a policy has been followed

inappropriate staff behaviour

the use of discretion (subject to next paragraph)

If a complaint involves HMRC’s use of discretion, the Adjudicator will consider the process relating to the exercise of that discretion and whether the judgement reached by HMRC is reasonable. The Adjudicator is not able to substitute their judgement for a reasonable judgement reached by HMRC.

5.11 The Adjudicator may decide that redress is appropriate in some cases. Any recommendation will be in accordance with HMRC’s codes of practice and policies on redress and the Parliamentary Health and Service Ombudsman principles and standards of good complaint handling.

5.12 The Adjudicator cannot look at complaints about the following:

government or departmental policy, including decisions to legislate.

matters arising from a commercial or employment contract between a customer and HMRC.

matters which have been considered by a court or tribunal or where there is specific right of determination by any court or tribunal.

matters that have been, are being, or due to be investigated by the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman.

the outcome of any agreement or settlement between a customer and HMRC including any agreement reached under an individual ADR.

matters falling into the remit of the Information Commissioner’s Office.

misconduct including those that could be considered by the Independent Office for Police Conduct in England & Wales or the Police Investigations & Review Commissioner in Scotland.

Valuation decisions of Statutory Officers in the VOA.

where the subject matter of the complaint is under investigation or enquiry by HMRC and where, by investigating the complaint, the Adjudicator could compromise HMRC’s effective and reasonable operation of its powers and published policies.

5.13 Sometimes actions by HMRC to progress a complaint will take a long time to resolve – for example where compliance activity or legal action is ongoing. In these circumstances, the Adjudicator will take account of this and comment only when they feel action has not been progressed within a reasonable timeframe.

Access to HMRC staff and records

5.14 The Adjudicator will have access to all relevant staff, information and data required for the consideration of complaints received. However, HMRC will have regard to paragraph 6.15 of the Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996 (section 23(1)) Code of Practice (see Appendix A), where HMRC considers that the information is sensitive.

5.15 The Adjudicator will use the same security classification standards as HMRC on data, documents and copies held within their offices.

5.16 On rare occasions, it may be necessary for HMRC to tell the Adjudicator that disclosure of a document would not be in the public interest. Should this situation arise, the Adjudicator and the AO will not make reference to the document or its contents in any communication with the customer unless otherwise agreed with HMRC.

Specific case requirements

5.17 Where the impact of the recommendation might be significant for HMRC, the Adjudicator will discuss their final recommendations with HMRC. Such cases will be identified through the AO internal process.

Adjudicator’s conclusions and recommendations

5.18 HMRC welcomes feedback and insights from the Adjudicator to identify opportunities to learn lessons, improve complaint handling and its service to customers.

5.19 The Adjudicator will issue the final report, conclusion and recommendations on individual case to the relevant HMRC Director or Chief Executive for VOA.

5.20 The HMRC Director or Chief Executive for VOA will be responsible for ensuring the recommendations made by the Adjudicator are implemented and any redress paid where appropriate. In the exceptional circumstances where the HMRC Director or Chief Executive for VOA have any concerns, they should discuss them with the Second Permanent Secretary of HMRC.

The Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Executive will decide if the case should be discussed with the Adjudicator.

5.21 HMRC is not bound to accept any or all aspects of a report, conclusion or recommendation providing that their decision not to accept is based on a fair and consistent application of HMRC’s published standards, guidance and codes of practice, with factual evidence of the complaint, and agreed by the Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Executive.

5.22 The Adjudicator and AO will regularly share with HMRC wider thematic learning through its reporting process, annual report, relevant board meetings and other channels. HMRC will provide regular feedback to the Adjudicator and the AO on action taken on this learning.

Where the Adjudicator plans to publish any report, they will share content and plans with HMRC and the VOA in advance.

HMRC service standards

5.23 The service standards to which HMRC will work in respect of this agreement are set out at Appendix B.

6 Terms of agreement

This agreement was last updated 27 August 2024. This agreement remains in force until such time as it is terminated as set out below. HMRC, and the Adjudicator will review the agreement every five years – the next review due in September 2029.

Variation

6.1 This agreement can be altered at any time by agreement between HMRC, and the Adjudicator to reflect changing priorities and opportunities.

6.2 At least 20 working days’ notice must be given by either HMRC, or the Adjudicator of any proposals to vary or change the conditions of this agreement.

6.3 All changes must be agreed in writing between HMRC, and the Adjudicator.

6.4 The detail of any changes and the timetable for implementing them will be shared and agreed by HMRC, and the Adjudicator.

Resolution of dispute

6.5 With the exception of matters where this agreement specifically states the decision is one for HMRC to make, any disputes or disagreements between the Adjudicator, the AO and HMRC relating to this agreement shall initially be discussed by the AO Head of Office, CPD Director or Chief Executive for the VOA, in consultation with relevant HMRC and VOA representatives.

6.6 If agreement cannot be reached, discussions will be held between the Adjudicator and the Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Executive. In the event an agreement still cannot be reached, the final decision will rest with the Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Executive.

Termination of agreement

6.7 HMRC may terminate this agreement for operational or other reasons. HMRC will notify the Adjudicator of the termination, allowing a minimum 90 calendar days’ notice from the date of notification.

Business continuity

6.8 Where the Adjudicator is unable to fulfil any obligations under this agreement due to actions or interventions of a third party (or third parties), or due to circumstances beyond the Adjudicator’s control, the AO Head of Office and CPD will agree alternative for business continuity for the duration of the difficulty. This will cover all/any AO locations, in line with HMRC security and business continuity policies.

7 Governance, access, resources

7.1 This section provides detail around the governance arrangements in place to secure and underpin the independence of both the Adjudicator and the AO in carrying out their role, and to clearly evidence that to customers, HMRC and external stakeholders.

7.2 The Adjudicator is independent or ‘at arm’s length’ to HMRC and their decisions are not subject to influence or interference.

HMRC

7.3 The Second Permanent Secretary will provide strategic ownership and overview on behalf of HMRC.

7.4 The Adjudicator will meet formally at least once a year with HMRC’s Executive Committee and HMRC Board to discuss progress, matters of concern and to share best practice.

7.5 The Adjudicator will be invited to attend the HMRC Board at least annually, and any appropriate Board Committee to keep them updated on customer issues and the HMRC response including:

progress on the Adjudicator’s role and vision

specific issues brought to HMRC’s attention

wider contributions on topics impacting on customers

7.6 The Adjudicator will meet regularly with the lead Non-Executive Director.

7.7 The Adjudicator will have direct access to any ExCom member or Director General as and when required to discuss issues relating to their area of business.

7.8 CPD will support the Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Executive, HMRC, the Adjudicator and the AO by being the day-to-day administrative contact for the SLA and any operational issues not requiring initial senior intervention or discussion.

7.9 CPD will be the initial escalation for any HMRC business areas on issues or disagreement arising from this agreement, or any other interaction with AO.

7.10 CPD will promote an HMRC wide understanding and appreciation of the role of the Adjudicator and the AO.

The Adjudicator

7.11 The Adjudicator will set the direction of the AO including performance, planning and value for money delivery of the adjudication services within the scope of the role and remit. These will fit with the requirement that the AO follows HMRC procedures and policies on financial propriety and management, personnel, data security and other matters.

7.12 The Adjudicator will set standards to ensure that quality and independence are maintained throughout the work of the AO.

7.13 The Adjudicator will publish an annual report covering AO performance, how HMRC has handled complaints referred by its customers, including learning from complaints and insights provided. The Adjudicator holds editorial control of the report and HMRC has no power of veto over the contents.

7.14 The Adjudicator will contribute insight into the Charter performance as part of HMRC’s annual Charter review.

7.15 The Adjudicator may request legal advice from Solicitor’s Office and Legal Services (SOLS). However, SOLS retain the right to refuse to act in instances where it would be inappropriate for SOLS to advise. In such instances, the Adjudicator may seek legal advice from the Government Legal Department.

The Adjudicator’s Office

7.16 HMRC will provide a support unit, the AO. This includes staff, accommodation, equipment and materials to enable the Adjudicator to resolve complaints referred by customers and provide HMRC with opportunities to learn and make improvements based on feedback, recommendations and insight shared.

7.17 The AO:

will comply with all the relevant HMRC policies, guidelines and processes on finance, personnel and data security and other matters,

will publish customer service standards,

is subject to the same assurance processes, including HMRC Internal Audit as HMRC offices,

is entitled access to SOLS in relation to non-contentious matters (statutory interpretation), and to Government Legal Department in relation to contentious matters and its own obligations,

will provide relevant performance data,

7.18 The AO Head of Office is accountable to the Adjudicator, on a day-to-day basis, for implementing the Adjudicator’s strategy and for delivering the services set out in this agreement.

7.19 To ensure the AO’s independence when supporting the Adjudicator, the AO Head of Office’s accountabilities and line of reporting to HMRC will be at arm’s length to the main operational delivery lines of HMRC’s business, from which the majority of complaints would be referred by customers.

7.20 The Director of CPD will have line management responsibility for the AO Head of Office who will have a matrix performance agreement fully reflecting the principles of this SLA, agreed with both the Director of CPD and the Adjudicator

Adjudicator’s Office staffing

7.21 The staff in the AO are HMRC employees and line management will flow up to and via the AO Head of Office

Freedom of information and data protection

7.22 For the purposes of the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the data protection legislation, the AO forms part of a single public authority with HMRC.

7.23 All requests for customer specific information under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 or the Data Protection Act 2018 (General Data Protection Regulation from 25 May 2018) will be recorded. The AO will work closely with HMRC, FOI and DP teams to ensure the appropriate policies and procedures are followed.

7.24 The AO will refer all requests for HMRC (or VOA) guidance, policy and non-personal information back to HMRC to handle - the AO will not release such information to customers independently.

Complaints from customers about the Adjudicator or the Adjudicator’s Office

7.25 The AO will provide clear information to customers on how to make a complaint about the way their issues have been handled by the AO.

7.26 Complaints about the services provided by the AO, whether directed to the Adjudicator, the AO or HMRC, will be reviewed in accordance with procedures set out in Appendix C.

Adjudicator’s resources and finances

7.27 HMRC will provide funding to cover agreed operational costs and provide relevant performance data for forecasting purposes.

7.28 In keeping with HMRC’s commitment to continuous improvement, the AO will seek to improve business performance in service delivery and value for money.

7.29 The AO Head of Office will agree an annual business case for funding with HMRC Finance copied to CPD. If necessary, discussions will escalate to the Second Permanent Secretary for resolution.

7.30 Any request for additional funding during the year will require a formal business case submitted to the Second Permanent Secretary.

7.31 Financial arrangements between HMRC and the VOA for the provision of adjudication services are set out in Appendix D.

Working with business groups

7.32 The Adjudicator and the AO will work directly with HMRC business groups whose complaints reach their office, providing appropriate management information and feedback to promote a learning culture.

7.33 HMRC will share data on the pipeline of complaints and appropriate management information to enable the Adjudicator and the AO to effectively forecast work and resource requirements.

7.34 The Adjudicator and AO Head of Office will work closely with CPD who have direct responsibility for customer experience, HMRC’s Charter and HMRC’s Complaints Strategy and will provide support to Second Permanent Secretary on the agreement and the wider cross government complaints agenda.

The schedule must include a statement that the disclosure officer believes the material is sensitive. Depending on the circumstances, examples may include the following material among others:

relating to national security

received from the intelligence and security agencies.

relating to intelligence from foreign sources which reveals sensitive intelligence gathering methods.

given in confidence.

containing details of persons taking part in identification parades

relating to the private life of a witness

Appendix B

HMRC service standards for working with the Adjudicator

This appendix sets out the service standards applicable to both HMRC and VOA.

HMRC will ensure in the final departmental response customers are made aware of the next steps in the complaints process, including the service offered by the Adjudicator and the AO.

During an investigation by the Adjudicator, HMRC will:

provide any subsequent information requested by the AO on open/working cases within 10 working days.

advise the Adjudicator and the AO of any delay to this commitment and keep them informed of progress. This could be where they are unable to meet this deadline because of exceptional circumstances or a particularly complex case.

discuss any difficulties with the AO and involve CPD/Chief Executive VOA if agreement cannot be reached.

After a complaint has been closed by the Adjudicator HMRC will:

confirm the recommendation has been accepted and inform the Adjudicator when the recommendation has been implemented, in exceptional cases, any decision not to accept or implement a recommendation to be discussed with HMRC Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Executive for VOA and an HMRC/VOA Director to explain in writing to the Adjudicator the reason(s) behind the decision.

implement recommendations where agreed as soon as possible/within 10 working days, unless in exceptional cases, the Adjudicator has been informed that implementation will take longer and told the reason for the delay

respond to suggestions made by the Adjudicator relating to departmental procedure and practice, setting out:

the action HMRC plan to take to implement the suggestion.

the reasons why HMRC plan to take alternative action and what that action will be.

the reasons why HMRC plan to take no further action.

provide any information requested by the AO in relation to resolved cases as a priority and no later than 10 working days.

Appendix C

Procedures for dealing with complaints about the AO and the Adjudicator.

General

A complaint is defined as any expression of dissatisfaction with the adjudication services provided, that is not resolved at initial contact and requires a response, whether the complaint is made in person, on the telephone or in writing to the Adjudicator, the AO or HMRC. This definition excludes complaints made by customers about any recommendations made by the Adjudicator.

Complaints about the services provided by AO

All complaints about the adjudication services provided by the AO and its staff, whether directed to the AO, the Adjudicator or HMRC, will be investigated in accordance with procedures set out by the AO. All such complaints are to be recorded by the AO and the relevant records made available for audit purposes.

The AO Head of Office will be responsible for ensuring that complaints are dealt with correctly and in accordance with the procedures and standards set out, including a full response to all issues raised with a separate, objective review of the case or escalation to the Adjudicator if necessary. If this cannot be achieved, the complainant will be informed about the role of the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman.

Complaints procedure

The Adjudicator will be required to maintain a documented complaints procedure and service standards statement that is visible to users of the adjudication services provided and all complaints will be registered in a complaints register which will be held at the AO.

If a complaint about the adjudication services provided by the AO is made directly to HMRC, it will be referred to the AO Head of Office promptly. CPD may ask for information about the number of such complaints and the actions taken to resolve them.

Complaints about conduct or behaviour of staff or the Adjudicator

Complaints about the behaviour or conduct of the HMRC staff of the AO will be dealt with by the Head of Office and his/her line management chain, following the procedures outlined in HMRC’s Conduct and Discipline policies.

Complaints about the personal conduct of the Adjudicator will be referred to the Second Permanent Secretary and Chief Executive for action.

Appendix D

Financial arrangements between VOA and HMRC for provision of adjudication services

The VOA will provide sufficient funding to cover a proportion of the full operational costs of the AO and the Adjudicator, to deliver the outputs shown in each AO annual business plan.

The arrangements for meeting a share of the full operational costs will be agreed between the VOA and HMRC Finance. The AO will provide any necessary estimates of costs to facilitate this. Such estimates will be based on the number of VOA cases settled as a percentage of the total cases settled by the AO in the most recent year.

If additional temporary or permanent staff resources are considered necessary during the year for the AO to provide the agreed level of service to VOA, the AO will prepare and submit a case to the VOA. If agreement cannot be reached, the Adjudicator and the AO Head of Office will consult the Chief Executive of the VOA whose decision on such matters shall be final.
